still_true: Wegovy's US list price is still $1,349 a month, and almost nobody pays it.
The FDA has approved no generic semaglutide or tirzepatide in the US, and generic liraglutide is still the only generic incretin on the US market.
The TrumpRx cash channel still operates, and oral Wegovy starting doses still cost $149 a month there.

The Medicare GLP-1 Bridge pilot has not been revived, Congress has not reopened the permanent obesity benefit, and Medicare still reaches users only through diabetes, cardiovascular, kidney, sleep-apnoea and dementia-risk (obesity plus established CVD) codes.

The September 2027 tri-agency guidance allowing up to 30% premium differentials tied to verified adherence still stands, Illinois's ban on adherence-conditioned premiums is still the only state ban of its kind, and the suicidal-ideation warning is still off the labels.

population.note: FICTIONAL. Arithmetic: 41.5 ever-used minus 29.8 current = 11.7 points of adults who used and are off now. Here are the flows from 2034. 4.0 points of new initiators: 2.6 still on, 1.4 stopped. The 15.4 points of 2034 first-course users: 10.8 still on, 2.3 stopped and restarted, 2.3 off. The 12.6 points of 2034 repeat users: 10.0 on, 1.2 stopped and restarted, 1.4 off. The 6.9 points of 2034 stopped-once: 2.2 restarted, 4.7 still off. The 2.6 points of 2034 cycled-off: 0.7 restarted, 1.9 still off. Current = 2.6+10.8+2.3+10.0+1.2+2.2+0.7 = 29.8. Off = 1.4+2.3+1.4+4.7+1.9 = 11.7. Restarters among current users = 2.3+10.0+1.2+2.2+0.7 = 16.4 (55% of current users). Cycled and off again = 1.4+1.9 = 3.3. Cycled share = (16.4+3.3)/41.5 = 47.5%. Stopped once and never restarted = 8.4. Persistence check: 2034's continuing users are weighted toward survivors (Medicare diabetic/CVD users and low-dose plans at ~55% 12-month persistence). Deliberate drug holidays by people who keep an active prescription count as 'on drug', and that raises measured persistence. New full-dose starters still persist near one-third at a year. Half of first-course stoppers restarted within the window, consistent with 36–47% restart within a year. Age check: 0.20×18.5 + 0.33×30.5 + 0.24×40.5 + 0.23×27.5 = 3.7+10.07+9.72+6.33 = 29.8. Income thirds average 29.8. 29.8% of ~276M adults = ~82.2M users, up ~5.5M. FICTIONAL payer mix: commercial ~12.8M (down from 14.5M under employer retreat), Medicare ~15.2M, Medicaid ~3.6M, DoD/federal readiness ~0.2M (≈150k active duty, ~50k Guard/Reserve), legitimate cash ~31.9M, imported or counterfeit ~18.5M. Sum 82.2M. Legitimate cash: ~14.6M cash weight users (absorbing many dropped by employers), ~10.6M licensed 'metabolic health'/longevity plans among adults without obesity, ~3.6M calm/focus (down from 4.1M after the consent orders and as flatness became a common complaint), ~1.7M Reset, ~1.4M AUD. Sum 31.9M. ~19M current users have a BMI under 30 and ~6.2M under 25. Adult obesity ~31.0%. ~18% of adults have obesity and have never used, still concentrated in the bottom third, the rural South and 65+ adults without qualifying codes. Pediatric: 12–17s ~2.9% (~0.73M of ~25.5M); 6–11s ~0.3% (~0.07M of ~24.5M), liraglutide plus semaglutide after the Feb 2036 approval, almost all in the 39 non-ban states. That is ~0.8M of ~73M under-18s, ≈1.1%. ~53% of children live in a household with a current user, and ~6.8M live with a parent who regained after stopping.

access.public_coverage: Medicare reaches ~15.2M users only through diabetes, CV, CKD, OSA and dementia-risk (obesity plus established CVD) codes, all behind prior authorisation. FICTIONAL arithmetic: 15.2M × ~$210 average net/month × 12 ≈ $38.3B a year in gross Part D incretin spend before rebate true-up, up from ~$36.5B. Users grew as the CVD/CKD population aged in, and average net fell $225 → $210 (~3.5%/yr). The dementia-risk route is ~2.6M × ~$220 × 12 ≈ $6.9B. Bimagrumab is excluded from Part D because its only indication is an obesity adjunct. Medicaid: six states still cover adult weight-loss use (one dropped in a 2035 budget), and ~3.6M Medicaid users are mostly on diabetes codes. After the Feb 2036 pediatric approval, families in several non-ban states are filing EPSDT appeals for children 6–11. Two state programmes still condition coverage on adherence and BMI progress. DoD's Metabolic Readiness Program supplies ~150k active-duty members through military treatment facilities: ~150k × ~$190 DoD-negotiated net × 12 ≈ $0.34B a year.
access.generic_rest_of_world: Indian generic semaglutide sells for $3–22 a month across 170+ brands. Chinese tirzepatide-analogue and 'reta' vials run $20–60 through research-peptide fronts. Canadian and Brazilian generic semaglutide is CAD 40–70 and BRL 140–240. India and China supply ~72% of world incretin volume. India's B2C export registration took effect in Mar 2035, and direct parcels were rerouted through UAE and Singapore consolidators and US domestic repackagers buying bulk API.
access.note: FICTIONAL. Employer weight-management coverage fell from 29% to 24% (Business Group on Health, Nov 2035) and to ~23% by late 2036. Most firms that left kept diabetes, CVD and OSA coverage, so coverage now sits on codes. Monitored metabolic tracks fell from 13% to ~11% of employers and from 7.4M to ~6.1M enrollees, all inside the 12.8M commercial users. ~4.8M of them are on clinic-administered MariTide, and total MariTide users are ~6.6M. Managed decline: TrumpRx maintenance prices are $169 for the Wegovy pill, $149–179 for Foundayo and $219–259 for injectable Wegovy/Zepbound; starting oral doses stay $149. Amgen cut MariTide's cash price $219 → $199 and Lilly cut retatrutide $299 → $279. Lilly's 'Keep' bundle (Zepbound plus bimagrumab, launched Sep 2035) is $449 a month cash on LillyDirect, against bimagrumab's $1,150 list, and ~1.4M people use bimagrumab combinations (~0.9M cash bundle, ~0.5M commercial). Amycretin is $1,199 list, mostly on prior-authorised formularies. Orals are ~52% of users. The gray market grew from ~15.4M to ~18.5M, including ~5M on 'reta' vials and a new trade in counterfeit 'bima' vials, which state labs found to be mostly saline or empty. Lifestyle spending account reimbursement of calm and Reset fees fell from 19% to ~15% of large employers after the Ohio ruling.

on_market_classes: GLP-1 agonist, weekly injectable (semaglutide: Wegovy/Ozempic; Wegovy now incl. ages 6–11)
GIP/GLP-1 dual agonist, weekly injectable (tirzepatide: Zepbound/Mounjaro)
GIP/GLP-1/glucagon triple agonist, weekly injectable (retatrutide, incl. 12 mg maintenance dose)
GLP-1 agonist/GIP-receptor antagonist antibody conjugate, monthly injectable (maridebart cafraglutide: MariTide)
GLP-1 agonist, daily oral peptide (Wegovy pill 25 mg; Rybelsus)
GLP-1 agonist, daily injectable (liraglutide: Saxenda, incl. generics)
Activin type II receptor antibody, muscle-preserving adjunct (bimagrumab), sold co-packaged with tirzepatide in Lilly's 'Keep' bundle since Sep 2035
indications_beyond_weight_and_diabetes: alcohol use disorder in adults (oral semaglutide)

pediatric obesity ages 6–11 (liraglutide incl. generics; weekly semaglutide approved Feb 2036), both with growth-monitoring and specialist-initiation language, and barred for weight indication by statute in eleven states
reduction of risk of all-cause dementia in adults with obesity and established CVD (tirzepatide; confirmed by 2035 trial)
muscle-preservation adjunct to incretin therapy in adults with obesity (bimagrumab)
mainstream_offlabel_uses: 'metabolic health' and longevity microdosing by adults without obesity (~10.6M on licensed cash plans plus a large gray share), now a routine line on concierge and executive physicals
scheduled 'drug holidays' and dose step-downs to manage flatness, built into platform apps as 'holiday planning'
compulsion 'Reset' plans for betting, shopping, pornography and screens (~1.7M licensed)
dementia-prevention use by 50–70-year-olds without CVD, cash or gray
bimagrumab bundles among normal-weight longevity users who are concerned about muscle, off-label and mostly cash
gray 'reta' and counterfeit 'bima' use in gym and longevity communities
drugs.pipeline_note: FICTIONAL. Two drivers are realised under the approval rules. Pediatric under-12: Novo filed an sNDA for weekly semaglutide in ages 6–11 in Jan 2035 on STEP Young data (~11% BMI reduction vs placebo at 68 weeks), and the FDA approved it in Feb 2036 with the liraglutide-style growth-monitoring box, specialist initiation and a 6-monthly height-velocity requirement. Muscle-preserving combination: no fixed-dose combination exists. Lilly realised it through existing products in a new form, co-packaging approved tirzepatide and approved bimagrumab as the 'Keep' bundle in Sep 2035. It filed a fixed co-formulation in Mar 2036, which is under review with no decision before 2037. The marketing line 'lose fat, keep muscle' rests on DXA lean-mass data, not fracture outcomes. The tirzepatide dementia confirmatory trial read out in Jun 2035 (HR ~0.86), and Lilly filed a non-CVD extension in Feb 2036, which is under review. Novo's gambling-disorder phase 3 is still running, with topline expected 2037. No new triple agonist is filed in the US, and Chinese triple agonists remain ex-US only. Implants remain in phase 2. US net prices drift down 3–5% a year, and brands hold ~$150–300 cash.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still the leading cause of discontinuation on full-dose regimens. New pattern: users who restart a weekly injectable at full dose after a 2–4 week holiday, without re-titrating, show up in EDs with vomiting and dehydration. Poison-centre and ED data attribute ~30k visits in 2035 to holiday restarts.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled; severe gastroparesis caution retained; 2036 label updates on semaglutide and tirzepatide added re-titration language after missed doses of two weeks or more.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Elevated with rapid weight loss; per-user risk unchanged.
Still no causal confirmation of acute pancreatitis; absolute risk low. The first EPI bellwether (Mar 2035) returned a defence verdict, and a second is set for 2037.

safety_ledger.effect: Lean mass (muscle) loss and bone-density loss
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Medicare hip-fracture HR holds at ~1.3 in users 65+ after more than 2 years and ~1.45 after three or more cycles. Bimagrumab co-therapy roughly halves lean-mass loss on DXA in the registration data, but no fracture outcome data exist, and 65+ users are mostly on Medicare, which does not cover it.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class warning (2028) retained; the FDA sent Lilly an untitled letter (Feb 2036) objecting to 'frailty solved' social copy, which Lilly withdrew; 'keep muscle' remains.

safety_ledger.effect: NAION (non-arteritic anterior ischaemic optic neuropathy) and related optic-nerve events
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Pooled FDA Sentinel and Nordic registry analysis (~6.4M users) found an HR of ~2.1 for NAION across GLP-1 receptor agonists, highest in users with diabetes and in the first year. Absolute risk is still low, at roughly 1–2 extra cases per 10,000 person-years in users over 50. That is an estimated ~2,500–4,000 excess cases a year nationally. Most cases leave permanent partial vision loss in one eye.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Jul 2035 class warning in Warnings and Precautions on all GLP-1 receptor agonist labels, with advice to stop on sudden painless vision loss. It is not boxed. In Sep 2035 FAA added baseline and annual eye-exam requirements for certificated pilots on incretins, and DoD followed for aviators.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: No new signal in adults or adolescents.

safety_ledger.effect: Reward blunting / emotional flattening ('Ozempic personality', anhedonia)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Clinically meaningful anhedonia at ~7–8% of weight-dose users vs ~3% of controls, and ~10–11% on retatrutide. The 2036 interim from the NIH normal-weight cohort gives the first low-dose figure, ~4.5% vs ~3% controls, which is imprecise. Users report flatness far more often than clinicians diagnose anhedonia, and ~40% of current users say they took a deliberate holiday or step-down in the past year.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: No labelling. FTC–FDA consent orders on mood claims remain; the FDA is reviewing the NIH interim.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Half to two-thirds regain within 18 months. Short holidays of 1–3 weeks produce little measurable regain, which is part of why holidays spread. Regain is fastest among gray users cut off by seizures.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: None directly; it still underpins the chronic-therapy framing.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: B12, iron and vitamin D deficiency; fat-soluble deficiency with EPI; low ferritin in adolescent girls; monitoring now also required for 6–11s on semaglutide.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Annual panel language retained; pediatric label requires baseline and 6-monthly nutrition review.

safety_ledger.effect: Exocrine pancreatic insufficiency after 5+ years of continuous use
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: ~2× EPI incidence after more than 5 years of continuous semaglutide; partial recovery in about half who stop for 12+ months. Tirzepatide's 7-year excess remains small and non-significant. Whether holidays affect EPI risk is unknown.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Semaglutide class labelling retained; tirzepatide under review.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon effects beyond ~5 years; effects in children on drug for decades; effects of repeated cycling and holidays; effects in people without obesity
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: About fourteen years of semaglutide follow-up now exist. ~19M current users have a BMI under 30. The NIH normal-weight cohort has given only its first interim. Cycling and holiday effects on bone and pancreas are uncharacterised.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Pediatric PMRs extended to semaglutide 6–11; NIH cohort continues.

safety_ledger.effect: Compounded / counterfeit / imported product harms (dosing errors, contamination, substitution)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: FDA adverse-event reports tied to non-approved product passed ~70,000 by mid-2036. In Oct 2035 CDC linked Burkholderia-contaminated 'reta' vials from a Houston-area repackager to ~260 bloodstream and injection-site infections in 14 states and 11 deaths. Concentrated 'reta' vials drew tenfold-dose errors, and poison-centre calls are ~9× 2025 levels. Counterfeit 'bima' vials are mostly inert. No repeat of the insulin-pen event was confirmed.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: India's B2C export registration began Mar 2035. The FDA added an import alert on UAE consolidators. Four more state felony laws. Federal personal-importation enforcement is still weak, and a DOJ repackager prosecution is pending.

safety_ledger.effect: Growth deceleration, delayed puberty and restrictive eating in children started young
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: The liraglutide height-velocity deficit (~0.7 cm/yr in prepubertal starters) persists at 48 months with partial catch-up in those who stopped. STEP Young semaglutide showed ~0.5 cm/yr at 68 weeks. Swedish registry ARFID HR ~1.8, unchanged. Final adult height is still unknown.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Semaglutide 6–11 label carries the growth box and specialist initiation; the eleven state bans stand; EMA has not approved semaglutide under 12.

safety_ledger.effect: Bimagrumab adjunct effects (muscle spasm, acne, diarrhoea; unknown long-term effects of activin blockade, including in people without obesity)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Muscle spasm in ~1 in 3 starters and acne in ~1 in 6, mostly transient. Normal-weight off-label users are absent from the trials. Little long-term data.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled; postmarketing safety study required; no restriction.

food_and_beverage.state: About 49% of US households have a user. Snack and confectionery volumes are down ~15–17% from 2025 and sugary drinks ~13%. Dollar sales are roughly flat on price and protein lines. Holidays created a small counter-current: retailers report 'off-week' spikes in dessert and snack purchases in high-density zips, timed to holiday weekends and Thanksgiving. Zip-code planning is now standard at Walmart, Kroger and Albertsons. The longevity aisle of fibre, creatine and 'muscle support' products grew on the bimagrumab marketing.

alcohol.state: US spirits volumes are down ~20% from 2025 and beer ~13%. AUD prescriptions through EAPs and telehealth keep removing heavy drinkers. Holiday weekends show measurable on-premise bumps that do not offset the trend. More brewery consolidation; non-alcoholic drinks pass 5% of volume.

restaurants.state: Traffic is flat to slightly down. Portion tiers are standard, and upscale places in Charlotte and Austin now run 'holiday menus' for guests who say they are off that week. QSR value menus carry low-income markets. Military-town casual dining near Fort Bragg and Fort Cavazos reports smaller checks.

apparel.state: Plus-size specialists keep shrinking. 'Lifted-body' and structured athletic wear grow with the bimagrumab marketing. Resale and stretch serve cyclers. Uniform suppliers to DoD and large police departments cut plus-size orders.

fitness.state: Strength training keeps growing. Premium DXA-plus-coaching gyms sell 'Keep' bundle onboarding. Budget chains' lean-mass add-ons are standard, and ophthalmology chains sell 'GLP eye checks' at retail clinics after the NAION warning. Longevity clinics bundle labs, microdose prescriptions, bimagrumab and VO2-max testing.

insurance.state: Employer weight coverage fell to ~23%, and coverage now sits on diabetes, CVD and OSA codes. Pharmacy trend ~+5% after the exits. Monitored tracks are shrinking, and LSA reimbursement of calm and Reset fees fell to ~15% after the Ohio ruling made promotion data a litigation risk. Part D premiums rose again for 2036. Self-insured firms push dropped members to TrumpRx cash links in their benefits portals.

pharma.state: Volume is growing and US net prices are drifting down. Lilly leads cash with retatrutide and the Keep bundle. Novo holds orals, AUD and the new pediatric label. Amgen loses employer-track share as employers exit. DoD contracts are small in dollars but valuable as an endorsement. Counterfeit-defence and litigation spending exceeds $1.2B a year. Indian and Chinese makers dominate world volume.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: The body still reads as payment route, but the bigger change is that being on is the default and nobody remarks on it. A lean, muscled body with a Keep bundle means cash or coached. A soft, slim body with a monthly bruise means one of the shrinking employer tracks. A body that has visibly put weight back on now draws one question, 'are you off?', and the answer it gets is a holiday, a seizure, a lost job plan or a choice. In the military, a uniform that fits after a failed tape test is the programme working.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: In Charlotte and Austin the status markers are biomarkers and DXA lean-mass percentage, and 'I stepped down to holiday dosing' is the new sophistication. Along the Columbus freight corridor, workers whose employers dropped coverage moved to $169 pills or gray vials. In Fayetteville, North Carolina, soldiers on the readiness programme and their spouses on cash Foundayo look alike, and the people who stand out are spouses who refuse it. In Memphis and the Delta, gray 'reta' and post-seizure regains still shape bodies. Upper-income parents in non-ban states are cautious about the new 6–11 label. Uptake comes mostly from families steered by pediatric obesity clinics and from EPSDT appeals.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Meals are shorter and protein-led. Holiday weeks have their own rituals: families schedule off-weeks around Thanksgiving and weddings, and caterers ask about them on RSVP cards. The Bread Alone fasting network has plateaued at ~800 congregations.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: Apps added a 'holiday-friendly' filter alongside lean-mass and biomarker verification. Disclosing that you are on is unremarkable. Disclosing that you never started now invites a follow-up question. Couples sync holidays for anniversaries and trips.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: For most users appetite has become something to schedule: muted most weeks, allowed back on holidays. In lower-income communities a returned appetite still signals lost access. Unmuted has moved from 'off nights' to campaigning against employer and military pressure. The MAHA wing attacks the FDA's 6–11 approval while many of its own voters take the pill.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Clinically meaningful anhedonia at ~7–8% of weight-dose users vs ~3% of controls, ~10–11% on retatrutide, and ~4.5% in the first NIH low-dose interim. A national survey (Mar 2036) found ~40% of current users took a deliberate drug holiday or step-down in the past year, with 'feeling flat' second only to cost as the reason. Platforms now ship holiday planners. Pilots and DoD enrollees cannot take unsanctioned holidays because stable-dose rules apply.
interior_life.framing: A known side effect people manage, the way they manage caffeine or a hangover. 'Flat week', 'holiday' and 'step-down' are everyday words. Clinicians call it dose-related reward blunting. Employers have mostly stopped calling it 'steadiness' in public. Unmuted calls it what the job requires.
interior_life.effect_on_work: In Nov 2035 a federal judge in the Southern District of Ohio denied summary judgment in the call-centre promotion suit, and trial is set for 2037. Two national call-centre operators and one large 3PL stopped using track adherence data in promotion decisions. Workers now ask HR for 'holiday weeks' the way they ask for leave, and some managers schedule critical shifts around them. The exception is readiness roles. Pilots under the FAA stable-dose rule, DoD enrollees and some police departments whose union funds pay for the drug cannot holiday without medical sign-off, and in those jobs flatness is part of the work.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: 'Holiday' became a genre: holiday-weekend festivals, off-week stand-up and 'off-week' episodes that streaming series schedule. Sportsbooks see handle spike on holiday weekends and dip otherwise, and they now market to the off-week. Ambient and slow games still serve the on-week. Flatness memoirs are common enough to have become a cliché.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Couples' therapists now routinely suggest dose step-downs, and synchronised holidays are standard advice for desire mismatch. A partner who refuses to holiday reads as a refusal of the relationship. Reset users who holiday face the question of whether the urge comes back.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: The pediatric approval split the restriction coalition. MAHA legislators denounce the FDA, while progressive advocates focus on employer and military pressure. Candidates in the 2036 cycle are asked whether they are on it. Admitting it is unremarkable; refusing to answer is a story. Veterans' groups and Unmuted lobby for a right to holiday in readiness programmes. Business lobbies still protect the 30% premium guidance.

state.regulatory_posture: Permissive on products, cautious on vision, hostile at state level to under-12 use. The FDA approved semaglutide for 6–11s (Feb 2036), added the NAION class warning (Jul 2035) and policed bimagrumab copy by letter. The eleven state under-12 bans stand, and the federal approval does not override them. Several AGs have said they will defend them. The seven-state in-person rules for low-BMI adults and the six-state off-label ad bans remain. The FTC–FDA consent orders remain. Congress passed only the defence provisions.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: FY2036 NDAA (Dec 2035) created the DoD Metabolic Readiness Program. Active-duty members who fail body-composition standards may enrol in oral semaglutide or tirzepatide through military treatment facilities, and the Army recruit pilot became permanent. Enrolment is voluntary, but it is the main route back from a flagged tape test. No civilian subsidy. TrumpRx remains manufacturer-priced.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: DoD enrolment ties drug fills to readiness records, and unsanctioned holidays are documented as non-adherence. FAA requires a stable dose for 3 months plus the annual eye exam, recorded on the AME worksheet. Commercial wellness-vendor data flows continue but shrink with the tracks. Two state Medicaid programmes still condition on adherence.
state.workforce_or_military: ~150k active-duty members are enrolled (~11% of active duty), concentrated in Army and Marine Corps. In Jun 2035 FAA moved incretins onto the AME-issuable conditions list, and the Sep 2035 eye-exam rule followed the NAION warning. DOT's 2033 commercial-driver guidance stands. Police departments in Houston, Phoenix and Jacksonville pay for drugs through union health funds tied to fitness standards. Shift-work employers lean on TrumpRx links rather than coverage.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: India's export registration began Mar 2035 and rerouted rather than reduced flows, through UAE and Singapore consolidators and US repackagers buying API. Chinese 'reta' supply continues through peptide fronts. DoD requires US-made or Danish-made finished product for its programme, which Novo and Lilly advertise. The cash-to-generic gap is ~40–60×.

events.event: India's export registration for direct-to-consumer drug parcels takes effect; within months US seizures show shipments rerouted through Dubai and Singapore consolidators and domestic repackagers, and in October CDC links contaminated 'reta' vials from a Houston-area repackager to about 260 infections and 11 deaths in 14 states

FDA adds a class warning for optic-nerve damage (NAION) to every GLP-1 drug label after a pooled analysis of 6.4 million users finds roughly double the risk; in September FAA requires pilots on the drugs to pass an annual eye exam

Lilly launches 'Keep', tirzepatide co-packaged with the muscle-preserving antibody bimagrumab, at $449 a month cash, under the slogan 'lose fat, keep muscle', and cuts retatrutide to $279; FDA later objects to social posts calling frailty 'solved'

Employer weight-loss coverage falls to 24% as large firms keep only diabetes and heart codes; the same month a federal judge lets the Ohio call-centre promotion suit go to trial, and two operators stop using adherence data in promotions
Defense bill creates a Metabolic Readiness Program offering incretins to active-duty troops who fail body-composition standards; about 150,000 are enrolled by late 2036

FDA approves weekly Wegovy for children 6 to 11 with a growth-monitoring warning, a year after Novo's filing; it remains illegal for weight loss under 12 in eleven states, and families elsewhere start Medicaid appeals for coverage

open_tensions: Readiness meets the eye warning. About 150,000 troops, a growing number of pilots and several police forces are on incretins under stable-dose rules that forbid the drug holidays civilians use to manage flatness, while the NAION class warning now requires annual eye exams. The first grounding or medical separation for optic-nerve loss in a programme enrollee has not yet happened, and no one has priced what it would cost.

The FDA approved semaglutide for 6–11s while eleven states ban weight-indication use under 12 and final adult-height data still do not exist. EPSDT appeals in non-ban states may force Medicaid to cover the children that the state bans removed elsewhere.

Employers keep exiting weight coverage. Displaced workers move to $149–259 TrumpRx cash or to an 18.5M-strong gray market that India's registration rerouted rather than shrank, and that market now sells counterfeit bimagrumab to people buying the 'keep muscle' promise.

Being off has become the thing people have to explain, and ~40% of users take holidays. Holiday-restart ED visits are real, while the effects of repeated short cycles on bone, pancreas and mood in ~19M users without obesity are unmeasured. The NIH cohort has reported one interim.

prose.headline: Off Week: Eighty-Two Million Americans Are On It, and Now You Have to Explain Why You Stopped
prose.world_in_600_words:
At the end of 2036 nearly three American adults in ten take an incretin drug, about eighty-two million people. More than two in five have tried one. The number grew slowly over two years, up less than two points, but the change in what it means was large. Being on the drug is unremarkable. When someone at a wedding takes a second slice of cake, the question is no longer whether they are on something. It is whether they are off this week.

That question exists because of the holiday. Flatness, the dulled pleasure people once called Ozempic personality, became an ordinary complaint, something people discuss at dinner and on the job. Four in ten users say they skipped doses or stepped down deliberately in the past year, most often to feel more before an anniversary, a trip or a holiday. Platforms ship holiday planners. Couples' therapists recommend synchronised off-weeks. Emergency rooms see people who restarted a weekly shot at full dose and spent the night vomiting, and labels now say how to restart.

Employers stepped back. Only about 23 percent still pay for weight loss, down from 29. Most kept diabetes and heart coverage, so access now follows diagnosis codes. Workers who lost coverage went to the TrumpRx cash links in their benefits portals, where pills cost $149 to start and $169 at maintenance and weekly pens run up to $259, or they went to the mail. After a federal judge in Ohio let a call-centre agent's promotion lawsuit go to trial, several large operators stopped using adherence records when picking shift leads. The 30 percent premium rule from 2027 still stands.

The mail is larger than ever. About eighteen and a half million people use imported or counterfeit product. India began registering consumer drug parcels in March 2035. The parcels now pass through Dubai and Singapore, or arrive as bulk powder at American repackagers. One of those repackagers, outside Houston, shipped contaminated retatrutide vials that infected about 260 people and killed 11.

In July 2035 the government confirmed what had been a rumour for a decade. These drugs roughly double the risk of a sudden stroke of the optic nerve. The risk is small, a few thousand extra cases a year in a nation of users, mostly people over fifty and people with diabetes. Every label now carries the warning. Pilots, whom the FAA had only recently allowed onto the drugs, must pass an annual eye exam.

The drug also became a job requirement in a few places. The defence bill signed in December 2035 lets soldiers who fail the tape test enrol in a readiness programme, and about 150,000 have. Police forces in Houston, Phoenix and Jacksonville pay for it through union funds. In these jobs the dose must stay stable, so the holiday that civilians use to feel something is not available.

Lilly found the next sales line in muscle. Its Keep bundle pairs tirzepatide with bimagrumab, an antibody that limits muscle loss, for $449 a month in cash, under the slogan lose fat, keep muscle. Regulators objected when social posts said frailty was solved. No fracture data exist yet. Lean longevity clients, now more than ten million on licensed plans and many more on vials, buy it anyway.

In February 2036 the FDA approved weekly Wegovy for children six to eleven, with a warning about growth. Eleven states still ban it for weight loss under twelve. Elsewhere, pediatric clinics begin cautiously, and poorer families file Medicaid appeals for it. The list price on the Wegovy box is still $1,349, and nobody pays it.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Marcus Tillery wakes at 4:50 in Concord, North Carolina, and does not take the Foundayo. Today is the eye appointment, and the ophthalmologist said to come in fasting for the bloodwork the AME also wants. The pill bottle says $169 on the TrumpRx sticker. The airline stopped covering it in January and put a link in the benefits portal.

The clinic is in a strip mall between a creatine shop and a dentist. A technician puts his chin on the rest. A green light, then a red one. 'Both optic discs look fine,' the doctor says, and signs the FAA form with a pen she's had to replace twice this month.

In the car he texts Renee: clear. She sends back a thumbs-up and then, a minute later: 'Holiday for Myrtle?' Their anniversary is the second week of June. Last year she stepped down for it. He can't. Stable dose, three months, it's on the worksheet. He types 'you go ahead' and deletes it and types 'we'll see.'

At the gate in Charlotte the captain, a man he's flown with twice, is eating almonds one at a time. 'Eye thing?' 'Eye thing.' 'Mine's in August.'

They fly to Columbus and back. The cabin is quiet. Somebody in 14C has a whole sleeve of cookies, and two flight attendants notice.

At home, his daughter Zoe, ten, is doing a worksheet on fractions. The pediatrician mentioned the new shot at her checkup and handed Renee a pamphlet about growth charts. It's on the fridge, under a magnet from Myrtle Beach.

He takes the pill at nine. It doesn't taste like anything.
